summary_en: Striders will acquire 100% of block party through simplified share exchange, issuing 597,600 common shares. The transaction is scheduled to be effective October 30, 2026. block party provides web application development, IT consulting, and system integration services; the acquisition aims to internalize IT outsourcing costs, strengthen IT/DX support for portfolio companies, and consolidate the technical expertise of representative Kouta Mitsuda.
title_en: Notice Regarding Complete Subsidiary Status of block party Co., Ltd. through Simplified Share Exchange
translation_en_brief:
Striders will acquire 100% of block party Co., Ltd. through a simplified share exchange, effective October 30, 2026 (planned). Striders will issue 597,600 common shares in exchange. The transaction ratio is 1 share of Striders to 16,600 shares of block party. As the transaction meets statutory thresholds, Striders does not require shareholder approval under the simplified share exchange procedure under Article 796(2) of the Companies Act, while block party shareholders' approval is obtained through statutory deemed resolution.

block party develops and operates web applications and provides IT consulting and system integration services. Its competitive strength derives largely from the technical expertise and customer relationships of representative director Kouta Mitsuda. Striders intends to internalize portions of IT-related work previously outsourced to external vendors, enhance its ability to provide IT and digital transformation support to portfolio companies and acquisition targets during post-merger integration, and systematize and deploy the technical know-how accumulated by Mitsuda across the group. The transaction is conditional upon block party separating its food and beverage business into a separate entity beforehand, so that it specializes in IT services at the time of the exchange. Striders plans to structure the ongoing engagement of Mitsuda for a minimum of five years through a supplementary technology transfer and business cooperation agreement, to gradually reduce the company's dependence on a single individual and strengthen business continuity.
